items.name: Proposition D.1.3 — vanishing off the middle degree (Caraiani–Scholze without the similitude restrictions)
items.statement: Let N ≥ 1, let Σ⁺ be a finite set of nonarchimedean places of F⁺ containing Σ⁺_bad, let V be a standard indefinite hermitian space over F of dimension N such that V_v is split for v ∉ Σ⁺_∞ ∪ Σ⁺, and let φ : 𝕋_N^{Σ⁺} → F̄_ℓ be a homomorphism. Suppose that F⁺ ≠ ℚ and that there exists a place w of F⁺ not in Σ⁺ ∪ Σ⁺_ℓ that splits in F such that φ is decomposed generic at w. Then H^i_ét(Sh(V,K)_{F̄}, F̄_ℓ)_{ker φ} = 0 for every integer i ≠ N − 1 and every object K ∈ 𝔎(V) of the form K_{Σ⁺} × ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺} U(Λ)(O_{F⁺_v}) for a self-dual ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺} O_{F_v}-lattice Λ in V ⊗_F 𝔸_F^{Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺}.
items.locator: §D.1, Proposition D.1.3, published p. 365; proof p. 366–368
items.note: Published label Proposition D.1.3 (arXiv v1/v2: Theorem D.1.3). When F contains an imaginary quadratic field and every place of Σ⁺ splits in F, it follows from Case 2 of [12, Theorem 6.3.1(2)] for the unitary similitude group. In general the proof is a sketch: pass to the Hodge-type datum (G × T, h × h_Φ), modify [12, Theorem 5.2.3/Corollary 5.2.5] for the honest unitary group, use [71, Corollary 4.7] and the association claim of [72, Proposition 1.4] with test functions φ_Σ ⊗ φ^Σ, and conclude that the argument towards [12, Theorem 6.3.1(2)] only uses [12, Theorem 5.5.7]. The proof as written assumes that K_{w_0,0} = ∏_{v|w_0}U(Λ)(O_{F⁺_v}) is hyperspecial, i.e. that no place of F⁺ above the rational prime w_0 below w lies in Σ⁺ — not a hypothesis of the statement (issue). Intro (p. 110) refers to it as 'Proposition D.1.3'. Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: Caraiani–Scholze [12]: generic part of cohomology of compact unitary Shimura varieties (cited)
items.statement: (As used) For a compact unitary (similitude) Shimura variety attached to a CM field F containing an imaginary quadratic field, with the relevant places split, and a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra that is decomposed generic, the localized F̄_ℓ-cohomology vanishes outside the middle degree (Case 2 of [12, Theorem 6.3.1(2)]); the argument towards [12, Theorem 6.3.1(2)] only uses [12, Theorem 5.5.7], and the discussion of [12] outside §5 is valid for all proper Shimura varieties of Hodge type.
items.locator: §D.1, proof of Proposition D.1.3, published p. 366–368
items.note: Black box from Caraiani–Scholze, Ann. of Math. 186 (2017). The paper's use: reduction of Proposition D.1.3 to [12, Theorem 5.5.7] after modifying [12, §5] (Mantovan formula and trace formula for Igusa varieties). Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: Auxiliary Hodge-type Shimura datum (G̃, h̃) = (G × T, h × h_Φ) and its integral model
items.statement: In the proof of Proposition D.1.3: let w_0 be the rational prime under w and fix ℂ ≃ Q̄_{w_0} inducing w. G := Res_{F⁺/ℚ}U(V) with Deligne homomorphism h (§3.2); K_{w_0,0} := ∏_{v|w_0} U(Λ)(O_{F⁺_v}) (asserted hyperspecial in G(ℚ_{w_0})). Fix a character ϖ : F^×\𝔸_F^× → ℂ^× unramified outside Σ⁺ with ϖ|_{𝔸_{F⁺}^×} = η_{F/F⁺}; Σ := {p | Σ⁺_p ∩ Σ⁺ ≠ ∅}. T ⊆ Res_{F/ℚ}𝔾_m is the torus with T(R) = {a ∈ F ⊗_ℚ R | Nm_{F/F⁺}a ∈ R^×}. Fix a CM type Φ containing τ_∞ such that all elements of Φ inducing the place w of F⁺ induce the same place of F, and a sufficiently small K_T ⊆ T(𝔸^∞) with (K_T)_p maximal for p ∉ Σ; Φ gives h_Φ : Res_{ℂ/ℝ}𝔾_m → T ⊗_ℚ ℝ; 𝔗 := T(𝔸^{∞,w_0})/T(ℤ_{(w_0)})K_T^{w_0} (cf. Definition 3.5.5). Then (G̃, h̃) := (G × T, h × h_Φ) is a Shimura datum of Hodge type with reflex field F.F_Φ ⊆ ℂ; for sufficiently small K ⊆ G(𝔸^∞), Sh(G̃, h̃)_{K×K_T} is smooth projective over F.F_Φ (as F⁺ ≠ ℚ) of dimension N − 1; for K = K^{w_0}K_{w_0,0} it has a canonical smooth projective model 𝒮(G̃, h̃)_{K^{w_0}} over W(F̄_{w_0}) with a moduli interpretation similar to §4.2, and F.F_Φ ⊆ W(F̄_{w_0})_ℚ.
items.locator: §D.1, proof of Proposition D.1.3, published p. 366
items.note: B(G̃, μ̃) → B(G, μ) is a bijection of Kottwitz sets and J̃_b ≃ J_b × T. For K^{w_0} ⊆ G(𝔸^{∞,w_0}) and m ≥ 1 there are Igusa varieties 𝒥^b_{Mant,K^{w_0},m} (𝔗-schemes over F̄_{w_0}) and [H_{𝔗,c}(𝒥^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)] := ⊕_i (−1)^i lim_{K^{w_0},m} H^i_{𝔗,c}(𝒥^b_{Mant,K^{w_0},m}, Q̄_ℓ), a virtual representation of G(𝔸^{∞,w_0}) × J_b(ℚ_{w_0}). The hyperspecial claim needs Σ⁺_{w_0} ∩ Σ⁺ = ∅ (issue). Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: Stable trace formula for Igusa varieties of the honest unitary group (modified [12, Theorem 5.2.3])
items.statement: tr(φ | H_{𝔗,c}(𝒥^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)) = Σ_{(H,s,η)} ι(G, H)·ST_e^H(φ^H), the sum over equivalence classes of elliptic endoscopic triples (H, s, η) of G, using ϖ for the Langlands–Shelstad transfer; with representatives as in [12, p. 734] without the similitude factor this becomes tr(φ | H_{𝔗,c}(𝒥^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)) = Σ_{G_n} ι(G, G_n)·ST_e^{G_n}(φ^n) (modified [12, Corollary 5.2.5]).
items.locator: §D.1, proof of Proposition D.1.3, published p. 367
items.note: 'Can be proved in the same way as for [70, Theorem 7.2]' (Shin's stable trace formula for Igusa varieties), since the Shimura variety has a moduli interpretation as in §4.2 although (G̃, h̃) is not of PEL type. Asserted, not proved in detail. Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: Stable/twisted comparison I_geom^{𝔾_nθ}(f^nθ) = τ(G_n)^{−1}ST_e^{G_n}(φ^n) (cited)
items.statement: With 𝔾_n := Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n ⋊ {1, θ}: I_geom^{𝔾_nθ}(f^nθ) = τ(G_n)^{−1}·ST_e^{G_n}(φ^n) holds as long as f^n and φ^n are associated in the sense of [41, 3.2].
items.locator: §D.1, proof of Proposition D.1.3, published p. 367
items.note: Cited as [12, Proposition 5.3.1] 'or rather' Shin [71, Corollary 4.7]. The paper notes that at rational primes in Σ there is no explicit local base change transfer. Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: Associated functions for characteristic functions at Σ (cited from the proof of [72, Proposition 1.4])
items.statement: For the test function φ ∈ C_c^∞(G(𝔸^{∞,w_0}) × J_b(ℚ_{w_0})) of [12, Theorem 5.3.2], if φ = φ_Σ ⊗ φ^Σ with φ_Σ the characteristic function of some open compact subgroup K_Σ ⊆ G(ℚ_Σ), then for every G_n the function φ^n is associated to some f^n; for such φ, tr(φ | H_{𝔗,c}(𝒥^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)) = Σ_{G_n} ι(G, G_n)·I_spec^{𝔾_nθ}(f^nθ).
items.locator: §D.1, proof of Proposition D.1.3, published p. 367
items.note: Association 'shown in the claim in the proof of [72, Proposition 1.4]' (Shin, cohomological base change for unitary similitude groups), following an idea in [72]; the spectral identity uses [12, (5.3.2)]. The remaining argument toward [12, Theorem 5.5.7] is 'the same as on the GL-side' with these test functions. Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: Corollary D.1.4 — cohomological genericity for almost all λ
items.statement: Let the situation be as in §6.1 (Π a relevant representation of GL_N(𝔸_F), E ⊆ ℂ a strong coefficient field of Π, finite sets Σ⁺_min ⊇ Σ⁺_Π, Σ⁺_lr, Σ⁺ ⊇ Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr, and φ_Π : 𝕋_N^{Σ⁺} → O_E from Construction 3.1.10). Suppose F⁺ ≠ ℚ. Then for all but finitely many primes λ of E, the composite homomorphism 𝕋_N^{Σ⁺} → O_E → O_E/λ (D.1) is cohomologically generic (Definition D.1.1).
items.note: Published label Corollary D.1.4 (earlier version of this extraction: 'Proposition D.1.4'). Proof: choose a place w of F with Π_w unramified with distinct nonzero algebraic Satake parameters α_1,…,α_N ([16, proof of Prop. 3.2.5]); genericity of Π_w gives α_i/α_j ∉ {1, ‖w‖} (i ≠ j), which persists in F̄_ℓ for ℓ large; Chebotarev then yields infinitely many places of F⁺ outside Σ⁺ ∪ Σ⁺_ℓ, split in F, at which (D.1) is decomposed generic; conclude by Proposition D.1.3. Chebotarev must be applied to ρ̄_{Π,λ} together with the mod-ℓ cyclotomic character (issue). Used for (L7) in §8. Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: A place with regular unramified Satake parameter (cited, Chenevier–Harris)
items.statement: For Π relevant, there is a nonarchimedean place w of F such that Π_w is unramified and its Satake parameter consists of N distinct elements α_1,…,α_N, which are nonzero algebraic numbers. Since Π_w is generic, α_i/α_j ∉ {1, ‖w‖} for i ≠ j.
items.locator: §D.1, proof of Corollary D.1.4, published p. 368
items.note: 'As pointed out in the proof of [16, Proposition 3.2.5]'. The ratio condition α_i/α_j ≠ ‖w‖ is irreducibility of the generic unramified principal series. Missing: routed to a source of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (route 5).

items.name: §D.2 setup — Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr, V, Λ, K, φ_Π
items.statement: Let N = 2r be an even positive integer. Consider: a relevant representation Π of GL_N(𝔸_F); two disjoint finite sets Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr of nonarchimedean places of F⁺ such that Σ⁺_min ⊇ Σ⁺_bad, Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr ⊇ Σ⁺_Π (Notation 3.1.4) and every place in Σ⁺_lr is inert in F; a finite set Σ⁺ ⊇ Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr of nonarchimedean places; a standard definite or indefinite hermitian space V over F of rank N with V_v not split for v ∈ Σ⁺_lr; a self-dual ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_lr} O_{F_v}-lattice Λ in V ⊗_F 𝔸_F^{Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_lr}; and K ∈ 𝔎(V) of the form K = ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_lr} K_v × ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_lr} U(Λ)(O_{F⁺_v}) with K_v special maximal for v ∈ Σ⁺_lr. φ_Π : 𝕋_N^{Σ⁺} → Q̄_ℓ is the homomorphism given by Π, and ι_ℓ : ℂ ≃ Q̄_ℓ is fixed.
items.note: φ_Π is really the ℂ-valued (O_{ℚ(Π)}-valued) homomorphism of Construction 3.1.10; the paper then uses ι_ℓφ_Π, so the printed codomain Q̄_ℓ is a slip (issue). [ι_ℓφ_Π] denotes the ι_ℓφ_Π-eigenspace. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Definition D.2.1 — transferable open compact subgroup
items.statement: Let v be a nonarchimedean place of F⁺. An open compact subgroup K_v of U(V)(F⁺_v) is transferable if: (1) for every endoscopic group H of U(V_v) there exist an endoscopic transfer f^H_{K_v} of 𝟙_{K_v} to H and a compactly supported smooth function φ^H_{K_v} on H(F_v) such that f^H_{K_v} and φ^H_{K_v} are associated in the sense of [41, §3.2]; and (2) when H is the quasi-split unitary group of rank N, φ^H_{K_v} can be taken to be supported on a maximal open compact subgroup of H(F_v) (which is isomorphic to GL_N(F_v)).
items.note: H(F_v) means the points over F_v = F ⊗_{F⁺} F⁺_v of H, i.e. the group on which twisted base change functions live (GL_N(F_v) for the quasi-split U_N). Footnote 38: condition (2) is not needed for Proposition D.2.3, only for its application Proposition 6.4.1. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Inertial transfer φ_{K_v}
items.statement: If K_v is transferable, the function φ^H_{K_v} of Definition D.2.1(2) (H the quasi-split unitary group of rank N, φ^H_{K_v} supported on a maximal open compact subgroup of H(F_v) ≅ GL_N(F_v) and associated to an endoscopic transfer of 𝟙_{K_v}) is called an inertial transfer of K_v; the superscript H is dropped: φ_{K_v}.
items.note: Appears in Proposition D.2.3 as tr(Π_v(φ_{K_v}) ∘ A_{Π_v}). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Lemma D.2.2(1) — split places: every level transferable
items.statement: Let v be a nonarchimedean place of F⁺. If v splits in F, then every open compact subgroup K_v of U(V)(F⁺_v) is transferable.
items.note: 'Part (1) is trivial' (U(V)(F⁺_v) ≅ GL_N(F⁺_v); endoscopic groups are Levi-type, transfer by constant terms). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Lemma D.2.2(2) — hyperspecial levels: fundamental lemmas
items.statement: If v ∉ Σ⁺_∞ ∪ Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr, then (the characteristic function of) the hyperspecial maximal subgroup U(Λ)(O_{F⁺_v}) is transferable and admits 𝟙_{GL_N(O_{F_v})} as an inertial transfer.
items.note: Combination of the endoscopic fundamental lemma (Laumon–Ngô [45]) and the base change fundamental lemma ([41], Labesse). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Lemma D.2.2(3) — small levels are transferable
items.statement: If v ∈ Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr, then every sufficiently small open compact subgroup K_v of U(V)(F⁺_v) is transferable.
items.note: Condition (1) of Definition D.2.1 for sufficiently small K_v is [54, Lemma 8.4.1(1)] (Morel); condition (2) by [41, Proposition 3.1.7(2)] (see the proof of [41, Proposition 3.3.2]). Used in §6 (footnote 24) and §8. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Fundamental lemma for unitary groups (cited)
items.statement: (As used) For an unramified unitary group U(V_v) over F⁺_v with hyperspecial K_v and an unramified endoscopic group H, the characteristic function 𝟙_{K_v} admits as endoscopic transfer the characteristic function of a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup of H(F⁺_v) (suitably normalized).
items.locator: §D.2, proof of Lemma D.2.2(2), published p. 369
items.note: Laumon–Ngô [45]. Black box. Planned: EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.3 plans the fundamental lemma and local transfer, including Labesse's base change.

items.name: Base change fundamental lemma and local transfer (cited, Labesse)
items.statement: (As used) The characteristic function of a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup of an unramified unitary group H over F⁺_v is associated (in the sense of [41, §3.2]) to the characteristic function of the corresponding maximal compact subgroup of H(F_v) (for H = U_N: 𝟙_{GL_N(O_{F_v})}); and (Proposition 3.1.7(2)) for sufficiently small levels the associated function can be chosen supported on a maximal open compact subgroup.
items.locator: §D.2, proof of Lemma D.2.2(2),(3), published p. 369; also §D.1 p. 367
items.note: Labesse [41] (Astérisque 257). Black box. Planned: EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.3 plans the fundamental lemma and local transfer, including Labesse's base change.

items.name: Existence of endoscopic transfers for small levels (cited, Morel)
items.statement: (As used) For every sufficiently small open compact subgroup K_v of U(V)(F⁺_v) and every endoscopic group H, 𝟙_{K_v} has an endoscopic transfer f^H_{K_v} that is associated to a compactly supported smooth function on H(F_v).
items.locator: §D.2, proof of Lemma D.2.2(3), published p. 369
items.note: Morel [54, Lemma 8.4.1(1)]. Black box. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Indicator c_v for v ∈ Σ⁺_lr
items.statement: For v ∈ Σ⁺_lr, c_v := 1 if there are complex numbers α_2,…,α_r of norm one such that Π_v ≅ I^{GL_{2r}}(α̲_r^{−1} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_2^{−1} ⊠ St_2 ⊠ α̲_2 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_r) (notation of §C.1), and c_v := 0 otherwise.
items.note: c_v = 1 exactly when Π_v (tempered, by Proposition 3.2.4(1)) is the base change of a K_v-spherical representation of the non-split U(V_v) (Lemma C.2.4). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Normalized intertwining operator A_{Π_v} (cited)
items.statement: For v ∈ Σ⁺_min, A_{Π_v} denotes a normalized intertwining operator for Π_v in the sense of [71, §4.1]: an isomorphism between Π_v and its twist by the automorphism θ defining twisted (unitary) base change on GL_N(F_v) (possible since Π_v^{∨c} ≃ Π_v), normalized as in [71, §4.1]; tr(Π_v(φ) ∘ A_{Π_v}) is the corresponding twisted trace of a test function φ on GL_N(F_v).
items.note: Shin [71, §4.1]; cited, not re-defined in the paper. Proposition D.2.3 allows any normalized choice; the absolute values make the formula independent of the choice. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Proposition D.2.3 — dimension of old forms in the L-packet (indefinite case)
items.statement: In the setup of §D.2, suppose that K_v is transferable for v ∈ Σ⁺_min. If V is standard indefinite, then dim H^{N−1}_ét(Sh(V,K)_{F̄}, Q̄_ℓ)[ι_ℓφ_Π] = N·| ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min} tr(Π_v(φ_{K_v}) ∘ A_{Π_v}) · ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_lr} c_v | for any inertial transfer φ_{K_v} of K_v and any normalized intertwining operator A_{Π_v} for Π_v [71, §4.1], v ∈ Σ⁺_min.
items.locator: §D.2, Proposition D.2.3, published p. 369–370; proof p. 370–372
items.note: Proof (indefinite case only): Π is tempered everywhere (Prop. 3.2.4(1)), so every discrete π with automorphic base change Π is cuspidal and H^i[ι_ℓφ_Π] = 0 for i ≠ N−1; if some c_v = 0 then H^{N−1}[ι_ℓφ_Π] = 0 by Lemma C.2.4; otherwise Proposition C.3.1 and Lemma C.2.4 give dim = N∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min} Σ_{BC(π_v)≃Π_v} dim(π_v)^{K_v}, and (D.2) ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min} Σ_{BC(π_v)≃Π_v} dim(π_v)^{K_v} = |∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min} tr(Π_v(φ_{K_v}) ∘ A_{Π_v})| is proved by a quadratic base change F̆⁺/F⁺ to a definite unitary group and Shin's trace identity [72, (1.8) & (1.9)], taking square roots. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Proposition D.2.3 — dimension of old forms (definite case)
items.statement: In the setup of §D.2, suppose that K_v is transferable for v ∈ Σ⁺_min. If V is standard definite, then dim Q̄_ℓ[Sh(V,K)][ι_ℓφ_Π] = | ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min} tr(Π_v(φ_{K_v}) ∘ A_{Π_v}) · ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_lr} c_v | for any inertial transfer φ_{K_v} and any normalized intertwining operator A_{Π_v} (v ∈ Σ⁺_min).
items.note: Proof 'left to the readers' (slightly easier than the indefinite case): same argument without the archimedean factor N (π_{τ̲_∞} trivial by C.3.1(4)). Used with Lemma 6.4.2 to get d_unr = d_ram. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Vanishing of H^i[ι_ℓφ_Π] off the middle degree (proof of D.2.3)
items.statement: In the setup of §D.2 with V standard indefinite: every discrete automorphic representation of U(V)(𝔸_{F⁺}) whose automorphic base change is isomorphic to Π is cuspidal, and H^i_ét(Sh(V,K)_{F̄}, Q̄_ℓ)[ι_ℓφ_Π] = 0 for i ≠ N − 1. If moreover c_v = 1 for all v ∈ Σ⁺_lr, then dim H^{N−1}_ét(Sh(V,K)_{F̄}, Q̄_ℓ)[ι_ℓφ_Π] = N·∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min} Σ_{BC(π_v)≃Π_v} dim(π_v)^{K_v}, the sum over isomorphism classes of irreducible admissible π_v of U(V)(F⁺_v) with BC(π_v) ≃ Π_v; if some c_v = 0 the left side is 0.
items.locator: §D.2, proof of Proposition D.2.3, published p. 370
items.note: Uses Proposition 3.2.4(1) (Π tempered everywhere), Proposition C.3.1 (multiplicity one; the N discrete series at τ̲_∞) and Lemma C.2.4 (at v ∈ Σ⁺_lr exactly one K_v-spherical π_v, with one-dimensional invariants, iff c_v = 1). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Auxiliary totally real quadratic extension F̆⁺/F⁺ and definite V̆ (proof of D.2.3)
items.statement: Choose a quadratic totally real extension F̆⁺/F⁺ in ℂ such that every prime in Σ⁺_min splits in F̆⁺, every prime in Σ⁺_lr is inert in F̆⁺, and the quadratic base change Π̆ of Π to F̆ := F.F̆⁺ remains cuspidal (hence relevant); such F̆⁺ exists by the same proof as [71, Proposition 7.4]. Let V̆ be the standard definite hermitian space over F̆ of rank N that is split at all primes not above Σ⁺_min and satisfies V̆_{v̆} ≃ V_v for every v ∈ Σ⁺_min and every prime v̆ of F̆⁺ above v (it exists since [F̆⁺ : F⁺] = 2). Let Σ̆⁺_min be the set of primes of F̆⁺ above Σ⁺_min and Σ̆⁺ ⊇ Σ̆⁺_min a finite set of primes of F̆⁺ such that Π̆_{v̆} is unramified for v̆ ∉ Σ̆⁺ and every prime in Σ̆⁺ \ Σ̆⁺_min splits in F̆. Take K̆ = ∏K̆_{v̆} ∈ 𝔎(V̆) with K̆_{v̆} hyperspecial maximal for v̆ ∉ Σ̆⁺, K̆_{v̆} = K_v (under V̆_{v̆} ≃ V_v) for v̆ above v ∈ Σ⁺_min, and Π̆_{v̆} having nonzero K̆_{v̆} × K̆_{v̆}-invariants for v̆ ∈ Σ̆⁺ \ Σ̆⁺_min.
items.locator: §D.2, proof of Proposition D.2.3, published p. 370–371
items.note: Existence of V̆: the product of local Hasse invariants is 1 because each v ∈ Σ⁺_min splits into two places with the same local space and the archimedean places come in pairs. Primes above Σ⁺_lr become split in F̆ (F_v and F̆⁺_{v̆} are the same unramified quadratic extension of F⁺_v), so they lie in Σ̆⁺ \ Σ̆⁺_min. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Exact associated-Frobenius image in the normal closure
items.statement: With E,L,N,K,q,alpha,d,delta,g,e as in S23-closure and gamma of prime-to-ell order, G_(S,gamma)=q(N^alpha)⊂K^h. Therefore the equality printed in Lemma 2.6.4 holds if and only if q:N^alpha→K^h is surjective. The formula still holds when excluding any prescribed finite set of primes. It does not assert that the main GI(T²−1), j=1 hypothesis implies this surjectivity.
items.locator: Not in the paper: a corrected statement supplied by an earlier version of this extraction; Lemma 2.6.4, corrected proof obligation
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).
items.proofStatus: Exact replacement formula and mathematical proof supplied; arithmetic application surjectivity and independent review remain open.
proofSteps: Take an order-d lift sigma using S23-lift in the cyclic preimage. Since e=delta*g is the residue degree in F(m)/F+ for this Frobenius, sigma^e fixes F(m) and stabilizes FS. Its restriction to FS belongs to the ell-group K and has prime-to-ell order; hence it is trivial.

Every lift of gamma is n sigma with n∈N. Its e-th power restricts to q(Σ_(i<e)alpha^i n), since the sigma^e restriction is trivial. Frobenius compatibility in the unramified tower identifies this restriction with the Frobenius at the underlying F(m)-prime.
S23-norm identifies the set of these restrictions with q(N^alpha), which lies in K^h by q alpha^delta=h q.

Conversely, for v∈N^alpha choose n=e^(-1)v; then (n sigma)^e restricts to q(v). Import Chebotarev on L/F+ and choose a prime of L with this exact Frobenius representative, avoiding the finite bad set.

Primes allowed by Definition 2.6.3 but ramified in other conjugate branches of L do not enlarge the image: in their decomposition group modulo inertia, choose a Frobenius lift above the selected E-prime. It still projects to gamma, and its e-th power restricts to the well-defined Frobenius of the unramified FS/F(m) branch. Thus the same power computation applies.

items.name: One-sided rank-two localization with a distinguished class
items.statement: Let O be a DVR, π a uniformizer, Rn=O/π^n with n≥1, S a free Rn-module of rank two, v∈S primitive (v∉πS), and f1,f2:S→Rn linear. Suppose π^c Rn²⊆image(f1,f2) for 0≤c<n. After possibly interchanging f1 and f2, there exists a primitive t∈S such that f1(t)=0, expπ(f1(v))≥n−c and expπ(f2(t))≥n−c. A basis diagonalizing both maps is not asserted. For an actual abundant pair of Frobenius evaluations with targets π^m0(O/π^m), apply this after n=m−m0,c=4rR and use S25-norm for local cohomology.
items.locator: Not in the paper: a corrected statement supplied by an earlier version of this extraction; Replacement for the rank-two use of Proposition 2.6.7 (p.135) in Theorem 8.3.2 (pp.317–320); original general basis claim E2 retained as a gap
items.note: Preserves the stable item id and draft alias S25. Elementary theorem proved in this report, not attributed verbatim to the authors. Application is conditional on actual abundance and is separated into S25-consumer; no claim about existence of those Galois evaluations. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).
items.provenance: Continues cc-d67081 / PR #2181; published-version refinement by Codex codex-c83e7a.
items.proofStatus: complete mathematical argument and exhaustive finite-ring diagnostics supplied; independent review required; not formalized
proofSteps: Choose a basis of S and any integral lift A of (f1,f2). By S25-lift, C=π^c A^−1 is integral.
If both fi(v) belonged to π^(c+1)Rn, reduction of C A=π^c I would force π^c v∈π^(c+1)Rn², contradicting primitivity since c<n. Thus one coordinate has valuation ≤c; label it f1.
Apply S25-row to that row. Its primitive kernel vector t has the required second evaluation. Neither row combination nor replacement of the actual Frobenius elements is used: only a permutation.
acceptance: A=I allows any primitive v, choosing a row with unit value and the other coordinate vector for t.
A=[[π,1],[0,π]], n>2,c=2 retains v=(1,0) and t=(-1,π) without making them a basis.
The zero matrix with c=n does not satisfy the strict hypothesis, and v=πe1 is not accepted as primitive.

items.name: Bounded-image matrix has an integral scaled inverse
items.statement: Let O be a DVR with uniformizer π, fraction field K, n≥1 and 0≤c<n. If a square d×d matrix A over O has reduction Abar whose image contains π^c(O/π^n)^d, then A is invertible over K and C=π^c A^−1 has entries in O, with AC=CA=π^c I. This holds for every integral lift A of Abar.
items.locator: Supplied by an earlier version of this extraction (not in the paper): elementary proof refining the inference in Proposition 2.6.7, published p.135; proof in report §Rank-two replacement
items.note: Source refinement assigned to ES.4, not a claim that the printed paper states this lemma or that the baseline already implements it. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).
items.proofStatus: complete mathematical argument supplied; not independently reviewed or Lean formalized
proofSteps: Choose preimage columns modulo π^n and lift to B over O, giving AB=π^c I+π^n D=π^c U.
Since c<n, U reduces to I modulo the maximal ideal, so det U is a unit. Use L08 to invert U over O.
C=B U^−1 is integral and AC=π^c I. Determinants in the domain imply det A≠0; over K, C=π^c A^−1 and hence CA=π^c I.
acceptance: A=π^c I satisfies the claim with C=I.
The hypothesis c<n matters: A=0 and c=n give the vacuous image bound but no inverse.
No completeness, characteristic-zero or finite-residue-field hypothesis is needed.

items.name: Primitive kernel vector preserves the second error bound
items.statement: Let O,π,n,c be as in S25-lift and A a 2×2 integral lift of a bounded-image matrix. Write its first row as π^a(u1,u2), where a is the minimum entry valuation and at least one ui is a unit. Then a≤c, t=(-u2,u1) reduces to a primitive vector in (O/π^n)^2, the first row kills t exactly, and the second row evaluated at t has valuation v(det A)−a≤c. In particular its reduction has exponent at least n−c.
items.locator: Supplied by an earlier version of this extraction (not in the paper): elementary proof for Proposition 2.6.7, p.135 and Theorem 8.3.2, pp.317–320
items.note: Only one row is killed. Neither a basis diagonalization nor freeness of the full kernel is claimed. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).
items.proofStatus: complete mathematical argument supplied; not independently reviewed or Lean formalized
proofSteps: The image bound forces each row's image ideal to contain π^c, hence a≤c<n.
Divide the first integral row by its common π^a factor. Its normalized row has a unit coordinate, so t is primitive and is killed by that row.
The second evaluation is det A/π^a. In C=π^c adj(A)/det A, a cofactor coming from a first-row entry has valuation c+a−v(det A)≥0 because C is integral. Thus v(det A)−a≤c.
acceptance: For A=[[π,1],[0,π]], c=2 and n>2, t=(-1,π) has first evaluation zero and second π².
A=π^c I gives t=(0,1) and exact exponent n−c.
t need not form a basis with a preselected primitive v; with v=(1,0) in the first example their determinant is π.

items.name: Prime-to-ell unramified restriction preserves exponents
items.statement: Let M be a finite Oλ-module and h an automorphism with h^g=1, where g≥1 is prime to ell. The norm N=1+h+⋯+h^(g−1) induces an Oλ-linear isomorphism M/(h−1)M→M^h. For an unramified local representation with arithmetic Frobenius h and the unramified degree-g extension killing its action, restriction on H1_ns is this norm map under Frobenius evaluation. Thus evaluation after restriction vanishes exactly when the original nonsingular class vanishes and preserves its λ-exponent.
items.locator: Not in the paper: supplied by an earlier version of this extraction; Proposition 2.6.7 second paragraph, p.135; Definition 2.2.2, p.124; explicit normalization supplied in report
items.note: A source refinement of SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0/L2. The degree is g=ord(hγ), not the order of an independently chosen lift in a larger Galois closure. This local statement does not settle E1. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).
items.proofStatus: elementary norm proof supplied; profinite H1/Frobenius comparison remains the named supplier interface
proofSteps: e=N/g is an idempotent with image M^h. Moreover ker e=(h−1)M: one inclusion is immediate; for the other use (h−1)Σ(i h^i)=g−N.
Therefore the projection M→M^h induces an isomorphism on coinvariants and N is g times that isomorphism.

For a cocycle z and arithmetic Frobenius F, z(F^g)=Σh^i z(F). This identifies restriction to the degree-g unramified extension with N; the finite-module procyclic H1 comparison is imported from the local-condition owner.
acceptance: For h=1,g=1 the map is the identity.
For h=−1,g=2 and ell odd both source and target vanish.
If g is not invertible, M=Z/ell with h=1,g=ell gives a zero norm, so the conclusion fails.

items.name: One-sided localization retains the rank-one error budget
items.statement: In the setup of the proof of Theorem 8.3.2, suppose the actual (S,γ)-abundant pair has been obtained, with m>mper+mlat+mΣ+8rR+mdif. Put n=m−mΣ,c=4rR and choose the primitive v=π^mΣ s0 in S where π^mper s0=s as in footnote 33. After possibly interchanging the two evaluations, there is a primitive t∈S with loc_w1(t)=0, expλ loc_w2(t)≥m−mΣ−4rR and expλ loc_w1(s)≥m−mper−4rR. Consequently, conditional on the source's geometric reciprocity outputs, level comparison and perfect local pairing, the distinguished local pairing with its constructed c2 has exponent at least m−mper−mlat−mΣ−8rR. The error bound is unchanged; no basis containing s or v is required.
items.locator: Not in the paper: supplied by an earlier version of this extraction; Proof of Theorem 8.3.2, printed pp.317–320, especially footnote 33 and (8.11)–(8.14); replacement for E2 supplied by an earlier version of this extraction
items.note: Conditional repair of the E2 inference only. Actual joint Galois lifting E1, integral comparison E13 and the other geometric proof gates remain open; this is not a new unconditional proof of Theorem 8.3.2. items.proofStatus: mathematical replacement and complete exponent accounting supplied; independent review required
proofSteps: The evaluations of S land in the submodule annihilated by π^n in the free rank-one O/π^m target, namely π^mΣ times that target. Identify this submodule with O/π^n by multiplication by π^mΣ; abundance is precisely the image bound π^c(O/π^n)^2.
Apply localization-selmer to the distinguished primitive v. S25-norm transports exact zero and the two exponent inequalities back from evaluation to unramified local cohomology.
Use π^mper v=π^mΣ s, rather than a negative uniformizer power: since n−c−mper>0, scaling the nonzero localization gives exp loc_w1(s)≥m−mper−c.

Keep (8.12) and (8.13) with the same right sides. Pair t with c2. Vanishing at w1 uses only loc_w1(t)=0; no condition on loc_w2(v) is needed. The two losses c+c give 8rR, while mper,mlat,mΣ and mdif are unchanged.
acceptance: At rR=0 the replacement loses no additional λ-power.
The example A=[[π,1],[0,π]] is accepted even though no diagonal domain basis exists.
If mΣ<mper the identity π^mper v=π^mΣ s still avoids undefined division in the torsion module.

items.name: Normal closure and the actual restriction map
items.statement: In the setup of §§2.3,2.6 let E=F(m)+, K=Gal(FS/F(m)), and L the normal closure over F+ of FS E. Set N=Gal(L/E) and let q:N→K be restriction. N is a finite abelian ell-group; q is additive and need not be surjective. For gamma∈Gal(E/F+) of prime-to-ell order d and in the specified c-coset, choose an order-d lift sigma in Gal(L/F+); put alpha=conj(sigma)|N. Write delta=[F:F+], h=h_gamma on K through theta_S, g=ord(h_gamma on Rbar(m)), and e=delta*g. Then e divides d, q alpha^delta=h q, and q alpha^e=q. The fixed image q(N^alpha) uses additive groups, not an assumed O_lambda-module structure on K.

items.proofStatus: Mathematical argument supplied; exact Lean/Galois interfaces and independent review remain.
proofSteps: Every conjugate of FS E is abelian of ell-power degree over the normal field E. Restriction embeds N into their finite product, so N is abelian of ell-power order.
Use Schur–Zassenhaus only in the preimage of the CYCLIC group generated by gamma, whose quotient order is d; do not split the full Gal(FS/F) extension.
For n∈N, restriction of sigma^delta n sigma^(-delta) is conjugation by an element of GF whose action on Rbar(m) is h_gamma. The equivariance and injectivity of theta_S yield q alpha^delta=h q.

Gamma has order d; the least positive power fixing F(m) is e=delta*g, hence e divides d. Since alpha is unchanged by replacing sigma by another lift (N abelian), its fixed subgroup is independent of the lift.

items.name: A prime-to-ell cyclic quotient admits a lift of the same order
items.statement: For a finite group B with normal abelian ell-subgroup N and cyclic quotient B/N generated by gamma of order d prime to ell, gamma has a lift sigma of order exactly d. If tau is any lift, a=tau^d∈N is fixed by conjugation by tau, and sigma=(-d^(-1)a) tau is such a lift, writing N additively.

items.proofStatus: Mathematical argument supplied; exact Lean/Galois interfaces and independent review remain.
proofSteps: Multiplication by d is an automorphism of the finite abelian ell-group N. Thus d^(-1)a is defined intrinsically and is fixed by tau.
The correction commutes with tau, so sigma^d=-a+tau^d=0 in N. Its image has order d, forcing ord(sigma)=d.
Alternatively obtain a complement from the exact library theorem L09 in the cyclic preimage. This establishes existence of a prime-to-ell lift only, not prescribed powers in another quotient.
acceptance: For inversion on Z/3 in (Z/3)⋊C2, every lift of the C2 generator squares to one; no lift has a prescribed nonzero square.
If d=ell, C_(ell²)→C_ell need not have an order-ell lift of a generator.

items.name: Projected partial norm has the full fixed-point image
items.statement: Let N,K be finite abelian ell-groups, alpha an automorphism of N with alpha^d=1, gcd(d,ell)=1, q:N→K additive, and e a positive divisor of d such that q alpha^e=q. Put N_e=Σ_(i=0)^(e-1)alpha^i. Then im(q N_e)=q(N^alpha). More precisely q N_e=e q A_d, where A_d=d^(-1)Σ_(i=0)^(d-1)alpha^i is the averaging projection on N.
items.locator: Supplied by an earlier version of this extraction (not in the paper): refinement of Lemma 2.6.4, published pp.133–134; original setup §§2.3,2.5–2.6

items.proofStatus: Mathematical argument supplied; exact Lean/Galois interfaces and independent review remain.
proofSteps: Write d=e k. The identity q alpha^e=q gives q N_d=k q N_e by grouping into k blocks of e terms.
Multiplication by d,k,e is invertible on finite ell-groups. Therefore q N_e=e q A_d.

Use L10 over Z/ell^a with a large enough exponent annihilating N and K: the norm image equals invariants, and the normalized norm is the averaging projection. No O_lambda-stability of the Galois kernel is needed.
For every fixed v∈N, N_e(e^(-1)v)=v. This also gives explicit preimages for the reverse inclusion.
acceptance: For alpha=-1 on Z/3, e=d=2 and q=id, the image is zero although alpha² is the identity.
For alpha swapping (Z/ell^m)² with ell odd and q the first projection, e=d=2 gives the full target.
For trivial alpha on Z/2 and d=e=2, the norm is zero but invariants are nonzero: invertibility cannot be removed.

items.name: Two conjugate evaluations give a sufficient lifting criterion
items.statement: In S23-closure with delta=2, put P_h=g^(-1)Σ_(j=0)^(g-1)h^j on K. Then q(N^alpha)=im(P_h(q+q alpha)). In particular, if n↦(P_h q(n),P_h q alpha(n)) maps N onto K^h×K^h, the printed equality G_(S,gamma)=K^h holds. This is a sufficient joint-image hypothesis, not a consequence established here from GI(T²−1).

items.proofStatus: Mathematical argument supplied; exact Lean/Galois interfaces and independent review remain.
proofSteps: Group the 2g terms in q N_(2g) into even and odd terms, using q alpha²=h q. The result is N_h(q+q alpha)=g P_h(q+q alpha).
By S23-norm its image equals q(N^alpha); multiplication by g preserves subgroup images because g is prime to ell.
Surjectivity of the pair map gives every (v,0) for v∈K^h, so the sum map has all K^h in its image. Conversely its image is contained there.

A weaker sum-surjectivity hypothesis is already necessary and sufficient; the paired hypothesis is only a convenient sufficient condition. Mere separate surjectivity of q and q alpha does not suffice.
acceptance: For inversion on N=K=Z/3, both separate evaluations are surjective but their sum is zero.
For the swap on N=K×K, the pair map is the identity up to coordinate order and the criterion holds.

items.name: Schur–Zassenhaus complement for a normal Hall subgroup
items.statement: For a subgroup N of a group B, with N normal and Nat.card N coprime to N.index, there exists H with Subgroup.IsComplement′ N H. In the finite cyclic preimage used here, restriction identifies H with the quotient, so its chosen generator lifts gamma with the same order.
items.note: Only the complement theorem is built; identification with the chosen cyclic quotient is an adapter. This does not prescribe the power of a lift in FS. Library: Subgroup.exists_right_complement'_of_coprime at the pinned commits.

items.name: Finite-group norm and averaging projection onto invariants
items.statement: For a representation rho of a finite group G on a module over a commutative ring k with #G invertible in k, LinearMap.range(rho.norm)=rho.invariants and rho.averageMap=(#G)^(-1) rho.norm. For a cyclic group, invariants equal the kernel of generator action minus identity.
items.note: Apply over Z/ell^a to additive finite ell-groups. Do not assume the Galois kernel has an O_lambda-module structure. Library: Representation.range_norm_eq_invariants, Representation.averageMap_eq_invOf_card_smul_norm, Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.invariants_eq_ker_apply_sub at the pinned commits.

items.statement: For an additive subgroup H of G×K whose two coordinate projections are surjective, its coordinate kernels D_G and D_K admit an additive quotient equivalence G/D_G≃+K/D_K whose graph is the image of H in the quotient product. No coefficient-module structure or finiteness is needed.

items.name: Paired-evaluation obstruction data
items.statement: In S23-closure with delta=2 and ell odd, set A=K^h, P_h=g^(-1)Σ_(j<g)h^j, q0=P_h q and q1=q0 alpha. Let J=im(q0)=im(q1)≤A and H=im(q0,q1)≤J×J. H is swap-stable and subdirect. Its Goursat kernels coincide: D={x∈J:(x,0)∈H}={x∈J:(0,x)∈H}. Put C=J/D and let tau:C≃+C be the induced quotient-graph automorphism; tau²=1. Define C^-={c∈C:tau(c)=-c}. All are additive groups; K and J are not assumed O_lambda-modules.

items.proofStatus: Mathematical construction supplied; independent review and formalization remain.
proofSteps: q alpha²=h q implies q0 alpha²=q0. Since alpha is an automorphism, q0 and q1 have the same image J.
Applying alpha exchanges the two coordinates of H, so the kernels agree. Both projections onto J are surjective by definition.
Apply additive Goursat L11. Uniqueness of the quotient graph and swap stability imply tau²=1. C^- is the additive kernel of tau+id; multiplication by 2 is invertible since ell is odd.

items.name: Exact anti-invariant defect of actual Frobenius evaluations
items.statement: Under S23-obstruction put G=G_(S,gamma)=im(q0+q1). Then D≤G≤J, G/D=C^+ where C^+=ker(tau−id), and x↦(xbar−tau xbar)/2 induces J/G≃+C^-. Consequently there is an exact sequence 0→C^-→A/G→A/J→0, and G=A iff J=A and C^-=0.

items.proofStatus: Detailed mathematical argument supplied; Lean implementation and independent review remain.
proofSteps: For x∈D, (x,0)∈H gives x in the sum image. Modulo D the sum of (x,y)∈H is (1+tau)xbar; every xbar occurs by subdirectness.
Since 2 is invertible, im(1+tau)=C^+; the projectors (1±tau)/2 split C=C^+⊕C^-.
The minus projector on J/D is surjective onto C^- and has kernel G, giving the quotient equivalence.
Use the nested-subgroup sequence 0→J/G→A/G→A/J→0. This sequence need not split.
Diagonal H gives a nonzero common quotient but C^-=0: full paired surjectivity is sufficient, not necessary.
acceptance: Diagonal, antidiagonal and independent-pair tests give full, zero and full sum image respectively.
The actual j=1 tensor GI hypotheses have not been shown to imply J=A or C^-=0.

items.name: A bounded additive obstruction gives a bounded evaluation loss
items.statement: Under S23-defect suppose a,b≥0 satisfy ell^a(A/J)=0 and ell^b C^-=0. Then ell^(a+b) A≤G. For e_lambda=ord_lambda(ell) and kappa=e_lambda(a+b), span_O(theta_S(G)) contains lambda^kappa span_O(theta_S(A)). Thus an input inclusion lambda^c0 Hom_O(S,Rbar(m)^h)≤span_O(theta_S(A)) gives lambda^(c0+kappa) Hom_O(S,Rbar(m)^h)≤span_O(theta_S(G)).

items.proofStatus: Detailed mathematical argument supplied; Lean implementation and independent review remain.
proofSteps: For x∈A, ell^a x lies in J and its class in J/G is killed by ell^b. Hence ell^(a+b)x∈G.
Theta is additive, so theta(ell^(a+b)x)=ell^(a+b)theta(x). Take O-spans only AFTER this inclusion; no O-action on the Galois group is assumed.
In O_lambda, ell is a unit times π^e_lambda, so the scalar-generated submodules coincide.
The sum a+b cannot generally be replaced by max(a,b): A=Z/ell², J=ell A, H antidiagonal in J² has G=0 and a=b=1.
Finiteness at each m supplies some a,b, but a uniform arithmetic error bound requires a+b bounded independently of m. This has not been deduced from GI.

items.name: Choose actual evaluation rows without enlarging the loss
items.statement: Let O be a DVR with uniformizer π, n>c≥0, r≥1 and R_n=O/π^n. If a set T⊆R_n^r has R_n-span M containing π^c R_n^r, there are r elements t1,…,tr of T such that the square matrix W with these rows has image containing π^c R_n^r. These rows belong to T; they are not arbitrary linear combinations replacing actual Frobenius elements.

items.proofStatus: Detailed mathematical argument supplied; Lean implementation and independent review remain.
proofSteps: The inverse image Mtilde⊆O^r contains π^c O^r and has rank r. L12 supplies Smith bases with coefficients unit times π^a_i, 0≤a_i≤c<n.
Thus M=Mtilde/π^n O^r≃⊕_i O/π^(n−a_i), so M/πM has residue-field dimension r. Select r elements of T whose images form a basis.
Their row-span U satisfies M=U+πM. Iterating n times, since π^n M=0, gives U=M.
There is B over R_n with B W=π^c I. Lift B,W to O: Bhat What=π^c I+π^n D=π^c Uhat, with Uhat=I+π^(n−c)D invertible by its unit determinant.
What is invertible over Frac(O). The integral matrix Chat=Uhat^(-1)Bhat satisfies Chat What=π^c I, hence What Chat=π^c I as well. Reduction proves the column-image inclusion with the same c.
No target row operations change the selected evaluations. Smith bases and matrix inverses prove their bound only.
acceptance: The bound is c, not r*c.
The strict inequality c<n excludes vacuous containment without r minimal generators.
The embedded program tests every three-element row set over Z/4 and Z/9.

items.name: Abundant tuples with an explicit Frobenius-defect loss
items.statement: Retain S24's injection, absolute irreducibility and free rank-one invariant hypotheses, with ell odd and delta=2. Let S be free of rank r≥1 over O/π^n, n=m−mSigma, and set c0=f(r)rR, f(0)=f(1)=1 and f(r+1)=2(f(r)+1) for r≥1. Suppose S23-error holds with kappa=e_lambda(a+b) and c=c0+kappa<n. There are r actual elements of G_(S,gamma) whose evaluation map, after identifying the π^n-torsion of Rbar(m)^h with O/π^n, has image containing π^c(O/π^n)^r. S23 realizes them at associated primes avoiding any prescribed finite set.

routes.brief:
Siegel and PEL moduli problems, Part II: unitary Rapoport–Zink spaces, RSZ integral models and p-adic uniformization, shared with PAPER-ZHANG-21, PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B, PAPER-LI-LIU-21, PAPER-LI-LIU-22 and PAPER-HE-LI-SHI-ETAL-23: one roadmap owns the unitary integral models. This paper (Liu–Tian–Xiao–Zhang–Zhu, Invent. Math. 228 (2022), §§4–5 and Appendix A) adds their special fibres at an inert prime 𝔭 of F⁺ (p odd, unramified, ℚ_p^Φ = ℚ_{p²}) for hermitian spaces of rank N that are split (smooth case, §4) or almost self-dual (semistable case, §5), with auxiliary CM moduli 𝐓_𝔭 as in Rapoport–Smithling–Zhang.

Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 4.2.3: M_𝔭(V, −) → T_𝔭 is represented by quasi-projective smooth schemes of relative dimension N − 1 with tangent sheaf ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}, Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞}). Theorem 4.3.5: the basic correspondence S_𝔭 ← B_𝔭 → M_𝔭 has fibres B_{s⋆} smooth and isomorphic to the unitary Deligne–Lusztig variety DL_{s⋆}, with ι|B_{s⋆} unramified (the printed 'locally a closed immersion' fails in general; see the extraction's sourceIssues) and normal bundle ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}, im α_{*,τ_∞}); Theorem 4.4.10: for N = 2r + 1, inc^*_⋆ ∘ inc^⋆_! = T^⋆_{N,𝔭} = Σ_{δ=0}^{r} d_{r−δ,p} T_{N,𝔭;δ}. Theorem 5.2.5: 𝐌_𝔭(V°, −) is strictly semistable of relative dimension N − 1, the union of the smooth balloon and ground strata M°, M• meeting in the link M†. Theorems 5.3.4, 5.4.4 and 5.5.3: the balloon fibres are ℙ(𝒱_{s°}), the ground fibres are the Deligne–Lusztig varieties DL•_{s•} with the stated tangent sequence, and the link square is Cartesian with Fermat-hypersurface fibres. Theorems 5.7.7–5.7.8: intersections of two ground fibres decompose over Hecke strata Hk_j, and S†_{s•} is (p+1)(p³+1)⋯(p^{2⌊N/2⌋−2j−1}+1) points (Theorem 5.7.8(2) holds for even N only). Propositions 4.5.6, 5.10.12, 5.10.14 (special morphisms b_↑ from rank n to n + 1 on the Deligne–Lusztig fibres) and Lemma 5.11.3 (the resolution of M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} M_{n₁}; the exceptional stratum is the ℙ¹-bundle ℙ(pr₀*N₀ ⊕ pr₁*N₁), not a trivial one). Appendix A: admissible pairs and unitary Deligne–Lusztig varieties DL(V, {,}, h) with Proposition A.1.3 (smoothness and dimension), Lemma A.1.4 (Fermat hypersurface cohomology, with (4) only for pairs descending to 𝔽_{p²}), Proposition A.1.5 (Xiao–Zhu), DL• and the intersection number ∫c_r = d•_{r,p} of Proposition A.2.4.

Cover, in this order: the moduli functors with their Hecke and 𝔗-actions; the source schemes S_𝔭, S°, S•, S† as Shimura sets of the definite inner forms; the correspondences B, B°, B•, B† and their Deligne–Lusztig fibres via Dieudonné theory; the Hecke strata of §5.7 and the excess-intersection computations; the special morphisms of §§4.5 and 5.10; the semistable product and its blow-up in §5.11; Appendix A. Import PELModuli M0–M4 (PEL data, moduli, representability), AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 (Serre–Tate, Grothendieck–Messing), FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2 (Dieudonné modules), ShimuraCompactifications C2 (toroidal compactification for the non-compact case), EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.3–EDC.4 (Gysin maps, projective-bundle and blow-up formulas) and LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.7 (strict semistability, weight spectral sequence). The incidence maps, weight-spectral-sequence computations and reciprocity laws that consume these models belong to ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems, not here.

routes.title: The Gan–Gross–Prasad conjectures for classical groups: relevant pairs, Vogan packets, Bessel models and periods
routes.brief:
The Gan–Gross–Prasad conjectures for classical groups: relevant pairs, Vogan packets, Bessel models and periods, shared with PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20, PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21, PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-LIU-ZHANG-ETAL-21, PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22 and PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-25. Liu–Tian–Xiao–Zhang–Zhu (Invent. Math. 228 (2022)) needs one proved endpoint and states one conjecture.

Lemma 8.2.1: in the setup of §7.1, if L(1/2, Π₀ × Π₁) ≠ 0 there are a standard definite hermitian space V°_n with a self-dual lattice away from Σ⁺_∞ ∪ Σ⁺_min and (K°_n, K°_{n+1}) ∈ 𝔎(V°_n)_sp, hyperspecial away from Σ⁺_min, such that Σ_{s ∈ Sh(V°_n, K°_n)} f(s, sh_↑(s)) ≠ 0 for some f ∈ O_E[Sh(V°_{n₀}, K°_{n₀})][ker φ_{Π₀}] ⊗ O_E[Sh(V°_{n₁}, K°_{n₁})][ker φ_{Π₁}]; it follows from [6] (Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu, Theorem 1.8 and Remark 4.17). Conjecture 8.3.1 (weak arithmetic Gan–Gross–Prasad): if L(1/2, Π₀ × Π₁) = 0 and L′(1/2, Π₀ × Π₁) ≠ 0, there are a standard indefinite V_n and levels as above such that the graph △Sh(V_n, K_n) is nonzero in CH^n(Sh(V_{n₀}, K_{n₀}) ×_F Sh(V_{n₁}, K_{n₁}))_E/(ker φ_{Π₀}, ker φ_{Π₁}) (the printed 'for every prime λ of E' is vacuous).

Cover the relevant pairs (V_n, V_{n+1} = V_n ⊕ unit line), Vogan packets, the global period of the diagonal on unitary Shimura sets and its relation to L(1/2, Π₀ × Π₁), keeping Conjecture 8.3.1 a conjecture. Import JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison (the Part II of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison proposed for the global Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture) and AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.3; cycle classes come from MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.2.

routes.title: Selmer groups, continuous integral cohomology, and Iwasawa cohomology, Part II: Arithmetic level raising and Rankin–Selberg Selmer annihilators
routes.brief:
Selmer and Iwasawa cohomology, Part II: arithmetic level raising and Rankin–Selberg Selmer annihilators, for Liu–Tian–Xiao–Zhang–Zhu, "On the Beilinson–Bloch–Kato conjecture for Rankin–Selberg motives" (Invent. Math. 228 (2022), 107–375). Setup (§7.1): F/F⁺ a CM extension, n ⩾ 2, n₀ and n₁ the even and odd elements of {n, n+1}, Π₀ and Π₁ relevant cuspidal representations of GL_{n₀}(𝔸_F) and GL_{n₁}(𝔸_F) (Definition 1.1.3), E a strong coefficient field, λ a prime of E, R the Γ_F-stable lattice in ρ_{Π₀,λ} ⊗ ρ_{Π₁,λ}(n).

Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 8.2.2 (Theorem 1.1.5): assume Hypothesis 3.2.10 for n and n+1; if L(1/2, Π₀ × Π₁) ≠ 0, then H¹_f(F, ρ_{Π₀,λ} ⊗ ρ_{Π₁,λ}(n)) = 0 for every admissible λ (Definition 8.1.1, conditions (L1)–(L7)). Theorem 8.3.2 (Theorem 1.1.9): assume Hypothesis 3.2.10 for n and n+1; if λ is admissible and, for a standard indefinite V_n with transferable levels at Σ⁺_min, the Π-isotypic Abel–Jacobi class AJ_λ^{Π₀,Π₁}(△Sh(V_n, K_n)) of the graph of Sh(V_n, K_n) → Sh(V_{n+1}, K_{n+1}) is nonzero, then dim_{E_λ} H¹_f(F, ρ_{Π₀,λ} ⊗ ρ_{Π₁,λ}(n)) = 1. Corollary 8.2.3 (Theorem 1.1.1): for modular elliptic curves A₀, A₁ over F⁺ without CM over F̄, not geometrically isogenous, with Sym^{n₀−1}A₀ and Sym^{n₁−1}A₁ modular, if L(n, Sym^{n₀−1}A_{0,F} × Sym^{n₁−1}A_{1,F}) ≠ 0 then the Bloch–Kato Selmer group of Sym^{n₀−1}H¹(A₀) ⊗ Sym^{n₁−1}H¹(A₁)(n) vanishes for all but finitely many ℓ. Corollary 8.2.5 (Theorem 1.1.7): the same for Π₀ Steinberg and Π₁ unramified with Satake parameter containing 1 once at a very special inert prime, both supercuspidal at some place, for all but finitely many λ. The corollaries' condition (c) reads 'F⁺ ≠ ℚ if n ⩾ 3', but their proofs cover only F⁺ ≠ ℚ (E105); take F⁺ ≠ ℚ, as §1.1 does. The unconditional forms rest on Proposition 3.2.11, which for N ⩾ 3 and F⁺ ≠ ℚ cites the unpublished Kisin–Shin–Zhu [37] (E30): state them with Hypothesis 3.2.10 as an explicit input.

Intermediate theorems to state exactly: Theorem 6.2.3 (odd rank: the Tate-class map ∇¹_𝔪 from E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪} to O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 is surjective, and E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪} is weakly semisimple); Theorem 6.3.4 (even rank, arithmetic level raising at a level-raising prime 𝔭 of depth m, under (P1)–(P6), rigidity, ℓ ⩾ 2(N+1) and cohomological genericity: the ground-stratum cohomology is torsion free, and the level-raising map induces F_{−1}H¹(I_{ℚ_{p²}}, H^{2r−1}/𝔫) ≅ O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]/𝔫; part (5), H^{2r−1}/𝔫 ≅ (R̄^{(m)c})^{⊕μ}, needs level-raising special modulo λ^m at every place of Σ⁺_lr (E89)); Proposition 6.4.1; Theorems 4.6.2 and 5.11.5 (the geometric reciprocity laws, Theorem 4.6.2 with the pushforward, not the characteristic function, of the graph (E51)); Theorem 7.2.8 and Corollary 7.2.9 (first explicit reciprocity law: the exponent of the singular part of loc_𝔭 AJ(Sh′_sp) equals the exponent of 𝟙_{Sh(V°_n,K°_sp)} modulo (𝔫₀, 𝔫₁)); Theorem 7.3.4 (second explicit reciprocity law: the exponent of loc_𝔭[Sh(V_n, K_sp)] is at most the exponent of 𝟙_{Sh(V*_n,K*_{sp,sp})}).

Cover, in this order: §2.7 (the conditions (GI^m_{F′,𝒫}), Lemma 2.7.1 with a common power, Proposition 2.7.2 with 𝒫 ≠ 0 and the corrected conditions on (a, b) (E4, E25)); special and very special inert primes (§3.3, with the reflexive closure of Definition 3.3.2 strong enough to give (PI3) at the Chebotarev step (E32)); the incidence maps of §§4.4, 5.8 and 5.11 and the localized analysis of the weight spectral sequence in §5.9 (Lemma 5.9.3, whose part (6) is proved only as an injection for torsion coefficients (E8), which is all §6 uses); §6 (level-raising primes, Tate classes, arithmetic level raising, with the R = T input); §7 (both explicit reciprocity laws); §8 (admissible primes, Lemmas 8.1.3–8.1.7 with the integral change of level (E13), and the two pairing arguments with thresholds m > m_per + m_lat + m_Σ + 𝔯_R + m_dif and m > m_per + m_lat + m_Σ + 8𝔯_R + m_dif).

Corrections the design must carry. Lemma 2.6.4 and Propositions 2.6.6–2.6.7 are false when [F:F⁺] = 2 (E1, E23, E2): the γ-associated Frobenius set is q(N^α), fixed by conjugation by a lift of γ, not the h_γ-fixed part, and it can vanish on one 𝔠-eigenspace; abundance does not give a diagonal basis. The proofs of Theorems 8.2.2 and 8.3.2 choose γ from (L5-2) without regard to S (E102): when R_ℚ ≅ R_ℚ^𝔠 (all of Corollary 8.2.3, and base-change pairs in the other theorems) a Selmer class in one eigenspace localizes to zero at every γ-associated prime. Repair: in rank zero take S in one eigenspace and choose γ of the matching sign; in rank one use γ at 𝔭₁ and a sign-flipped γ at 𝔭₂; for the elliptic curves of Corollary 8.2.3 the flip is multiplication by a central element acting by −1 on one factor; where no such element exists (Corollary 8.2.5, general admissible λ with base-change pairs) add a hypothesis giving both signs or supply another argument. The rank-one pairing needs only the one-sided rank-two localization, which keeps the threshold. Lemma 2.3.5(b) needs Hom_{𝔽_ℓ[Γ_F]}(End R̄, R̄) = 0 when O_λ/λ ≠ 𝔽_ℓ (E21). (8.5) and (8.14) at ℓ-adic places need Faltings' comparison (E106); Proposition 7.2.7 uses Liu's potential map outside its hypotheses, which the Part II SemistablePotentialMaps must extend (E93). No main theorem is shown false by these points; the design proves each with its repair or records the missing argument as a hypothesis.

Import: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 and EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (with the corrected §2.6 lemmas routed there); GlobalGaloisDeformations G7; AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.0–AG2.7; UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (the unitary integral models, basic loci and special morphisms of §§4–5, proposed alongside); UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators; PolarizedAutomorphyLifting ([51, Theorem 3.6.3]); SemistablePotentialMaps; GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups (Lemma 8.2.1, Conjecture 8.3.1); LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.7; EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a; IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.7 (for (L7) via Appendix D); MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.2. No norm-compatible Euler system is claimed.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 2.6.4 and its proof, published p. 134; arXiv v3 p. 19 (Lemma 2.6.4); arXiv v1/v2 Lemma 2.5.4(2), p. 19
sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 2.6.4 Suppose that the order of γ is coprime to ℓ. Then we have G_{S,γ} = θ_S^{−1} Hom_{O_λ}(S, (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}). … Consider the element (g^{−1}Ψ)h_γ ∈ Gal(F_S/F) = Gal(F_S/F^{(m)}) ⋊ Gal(F^{(m)}/F). … Since γ has order prime to ℓ, it is easy to see that there is an element γ̃ ∈ Gal(F̃_S/F⁺) lifting γ such that the image of γ̃^{[F:F⁺]} ∈ Gal(F̃_S/F) in Gal(F_S/F) coincides with (g^{−1}Ψ)h_γ.
sourceIssues.correction: Replace the equality by the inclusion G_{S,γ} ⊆ θ_S^{−1}Hom_{O_λ}(S, (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}). Exactly, G_{S,γ} = q(N^α), where N = Gal(F̃_S/F₊^{(m)}), α is conjugation by a lift σ₀ of γ of prime-to-ℓ order, and q is restriction to F_S. Equality holds if [F:F⁺] = 1. For [F:F⁺] = 2, the statement Proposition 2.6.6 actually needs is that the O_λ-span of θ_S(G_{S,γ}) contains λ^c Hom(S, (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}) with c independent of m. It holds with c = 𝔣(r_S)r_{Ind R} when R_ℚ ≇ R_ℚ^𝔠. When R extends to R₊ over F⁺, it holds for S inside a 𝔠-eigenspace ε exactly when γ acts on (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} ⊂ R̄₊^{(m)} by ε, and it fails otherwise (then G_{S,γ} = {1} if S lies in the other eigenspace).
sourceIssues.reason: Take F+=Q(√5), F=F+(i), ell=3, m=1, R=Z3(1), j=2 and the identity polarization (muΦ=1). Let u=(1+√5)/2 and S be its one-dimensional mod-3 Kummer class, coming from the integral finite unit class. F(m)=F(m)+=F(ζ3); its degree over F+ is four, so u remains a noncube (use the fundamental-unit description of Q(√5)). FS=F(m)(cuberoot(u)) has cyclic cubic kernel. Choose γ induced by complex conjugation, of order two; hγ=1. Complex conjugation fixes the real cuberoot and inverts ζ3, so every lift of γ has square one. All associated-prime evaluations are consequently zero, while the right side is the full cubic kernel. The Kummer/Bloch–Kato unit identification is an explicit external input to this arithmetic witness, not claimed newly formalized. Re-checked on the page image (2026-09-23): confirmed — checked on the page image of p. 134 (Lemma 2.6.4 and its proof) with the definitions on p. 133; the counterexample was re-derived independently, and the exact replacement formula G_{S,γ} = q(N^α) was re-proved. The lemma is correct when [F:F⁺] = 1 and false in general when [F:F⁺] = 2. Counterexample to the printed lemma (all hypotheses of Proposition 2.6.6 also hold). F⁺ = ℚ(√5), F = ℚ(√5, i) (ℓ = 3 unramified), E_λ = ℚ₃, R = ℤ₃(1), j = 2, Ξ the identity ℤ₃(1)^𝔠 = ℤ₃(1)^∨(2), μ_Ξ = 1, B = 1, so ρ₊(𝔠) = (1, 1, 𝔠). Fix m ⩾ 1; u = (1+√5)/2. S := ℤ/3^m·κ(u) ⊆ H¹(F, μ_{3^m}) (Kummer class) lies in H¹_{f,R}(F, R̄^{(m)}) (u is a unit) and is free of rank one (u is not a cube in F: units of F are μ₄ × ⟨η⟩ with η = u or η² = ζu). ρ̄₊^{(m)}|_{Γ_F} = (ε̄, ε̄², 1), so F^{(m)} = F₊^{(m)} = F(ζ_{3^m}); Res is injective by Lemma 2.3.5(a) (ε̄(Γ_F) = 𝔽₃^× ∋ −1 as ζ₃ ∉ F), so K = Gal(F_S/F^{(m)}) ≅ ℤ/3^m with F_S = F(ζ_{3^m}, u^{1/3^m}), which is Galois over F⁺. γ := ρ̄₊^{(m)}(𝔠) = (1, 1, 𝔠) has order 2 and h_γ = 1, so the printed right-hand side is all of K. Every lift σ of γ to Gal(F_S/F⁺) is τ·𝔠 with τ ∈ K, and 𝔠τ𝔠^{−1} = τ^{−1} (𝔠 fixes the real root u^{1/3^m} and inverts ζ_{3^m}); hence σ² = 1 and Ψ_{w^{(m)}} = σ^{2g} = 1 for every γ-associated place: G_{S,γ} = {1} ≠ K. Direct check: such places lie over primes v of F⁺ with ‖v‖ ≡ 2 mod 3, where every element of 𝔽_{‖v‖}^× is a 3^m-th power, so Frobenius fixes u^{1/3^m}. Mechanism in general: for [F:F⁺] = 2 the Frobenius at the inert place is σ^{2g}, and squares of lifts in the 𝔠-coset are constrained (σ² = (1+α)(n)·σ₀²). The step 'it is easy to see' asserts the opposite. (The displayed splitting Gal(F_S/F) = Gal(F_S/F^{(m)}) ⋊ Gal(F^{(m)}/F) is also unjustified, though only a prime-to-ℓ lift of ⟨h_γ⟩ is needed.) Relevance to the main theorems: in Theorem 1.1.1 R = R₀ ⊗ R₁ is restricted from F⁺, so H¹(F, R̄) splits into 𝔠-eigenspaces; for S in one eigenspace F_S is Galois over F⁺, σ₀ acts on K ⊆ Hom(S, R̄) through the action of the lift of γ on R̄, and G_{S,γ} = θ_S^{−1}Hom(S, (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ, γ=+1}); if γ acts by −1 on the h_γ-fixed line, G_{S,γ} = {1} and loc_w(S) = 0 at every γ-associated place, so no abundant element exists. Case for the defence: the inclusion ⊆ is correct; the lemma is correct for [F:F⁺] = 1, the setting of [46, Lemmas 5.7–5.8] that v1/v2 cited; in the Rankin–Selberg application with R ≇ R^𝔠 the needed disjointness may well hold, and in the base-change case one can probably choose γ with the right sign using the large image — but none of this is in the paper, which applies the lemma as stated. sourceIssues.correction: Take g ∈ Gal(F̄/F′) whose image (γ′₀, γ′₁, ξ′) mod λ^m lifts (γ₀, γ₁, ξ), and replace g by g^{ℓ^k} for ONE k that kills the ℓ-parts (the kernel of reduction mod λ is an ℓ-group) and is divisible by the d_α and by the order of Frobenius on the residue fields involved; then (γ′₀^{ℓ^k}, γ′₁^{ℓ^k}, ξ′^{ℓ^k}) lies in the image, reduces to (γ₀, γ₁, ξ) and satisfies (a)–(e). sourceIssues.reason: Choosing powers independently in the two representations need not give an element in the image of the same Galois element. Re-checked on the page image (2026-09-23): confirmed — checked on the page image of p. 136; the triple obtained by independent ℓ-powers of γ′₀, γ′₁ with ξ′ unchanged need not be in the image of the joint homomorphism. Powers of the components by different exponents ℓ^{d₀e₀} ≠ ℓ^{d₁e₁}, with ξ′ unchanged, correspond to different Galois elements. Defence: the intended argument is obviously the common power (as in arXiv v1/v2), and conditions (a), (d), (e) are Galois-stable (𝒫 ∈ ℤ[T]; eigenvalue conditions invariant under x ↦ x^{ℓ^k}), so nothing beyond the proof is affected. sourceIssues.reason: Freeness of source and target and a rational isomorphism do not imply an integral isomorphism: multiplication by λ on Oλ is a counterexample. P5 and the explicit compositions offer the missing integrality input; the full uniform construction remains to be written. Re-checked on the page image (2026-09-23): confirmed — locator corrected (it is Lemma 8.1.7, not a Proposition) and the correction sharpened to an explicit determinant argument using only the paper's own inputs. Torsion-free O_λ[Γ_F]-modules with isomorphic rationalizations need not be isomorphic: Γ = ℤ acting on O_λ² by (1 1; 0 1) and by (1 λ; 0 1) gives rationally conjugate, integrally non-isomorphic lattices (their reductions mod λ are a nontrivial unipotent and the identity). The integral statement is essential: in (8.7) and its rank-one analogue it transports the fixed exponent m_lat, defined at hyperspecial level, to the level-raised Shimura variety at a prime 𝔭 that depends on m; with only a rational isomorphism the lattice discrepancy could grow with 𝔭 and the final choice 'm > m_per + m_lat + …' would be circular. Case for the defence: every ingredient of the repair (the integral correspondences of Definition 5.8.1, Proposition B.4.3(1), intertwining genericity mod λ) is already in the printed proof; only the passage from 'nonzero' to 'unit' and the determinant argument are missing, so the lemma as stated is true. Independent check: Quotation checked on p. 307. The inference 'torsion-free, and isomorphic after ⊗Q̄_ℓ, hence isomorphic as O_λ[Γ_F]-modules' is invalid in general; the first reading's unipotent example is correct. It is not rescued in this setting. If H^{2r₁}_{𝔪₁} ⊗ Q̄_ℓ were isotypic for one residually absolutely irreducible ρ, every Γ-stable lattice would be ≅ T^{⊕μ} (O_λ[Γ] ↠ End(T) by Burnside and Nakayama, then Morita). But localization at 𝔪₁ only fixes the residual eigensystem, so several π₁ with distinct ρ_{BC(π₁)} lifting ρ̄ can contribute, and lattices in such a sum need not be isomorphic. The repair works, and I checked it. I° = T^{∘•}T^{•∘} ∈ 𝕋°_{𝔭} acts on each π₁-part by a scalar that is, up to a power of p, ∏(p + α_i)(p + α_i^{-1}) = P(−p)/(−(p + 1)). Its value for π₁ is congruent mod λ to its value for Π₁ (Chebotarev), and it is a unit because P_{α(Π_{1,𝔭})}(−p) is invertible mod λ (Definition 3.1.5(2)). The same scalar governs T^{•∘}T^{∘•} on the one-dimensional K•-invariants. Hence both composites have unit determinant on the free modules H^i_{𝔪₁}, and the integral, Γ_F- and Hecke-equivariant T^{•∘} is an isomorphism. The lemma is true; the integral statement is essential for the m_lat bookkeeping in (8.7).

sourceIssues.printed: For a rational prime ℓ (that is odd and unramified in F), we put R_α := (Sym^{n_α−1}_{ℤ_ℓ} H¹_ét(A_{αF̄}, ℤ_ℓ))(r_α) as a ℤ_ℓ[Γ_F]-module for α = 0, 1. Then R_α is an object in Mod(F, ℤ_ℓ)_fr of rank n_α with a canonical (1 − α)-polarization Ξ_α: R_α^𝔠 ⥲ R_α^∨(1 − α).

sourceIssues.reason: The polarization is induced from the Weil pairing on H¹ (a perfect alternating pairing on a rank-two lattice T); on Sym^k T the induced pairing pairs x^a y^{k−a} with x^{k−a}y^a by ±a!(k−a)! (or ±1/binom(k,a) if normalized), which is not a unit when ℓ ⩽ k = n_α − 1. Then Sym^k T and its dual (a divided-power lattice) are not homothetic Galois lattices when the image is large (e.g. ℓ = 3, n_α ⩾ 4), so no (1−α)-polarization of R_α exists. Defence: only large ℓ are used. Independent check: Text checked on the images of pp. 136–137: 'For a rational prime ℓ (that is odd and unramified in F) … R_α is an object in Mod(F, ℤ_ℓ)_fr of rank n_α with a canonical (1 − α)-polarization'. A_α is defined over F⁺, so R_α^𝔠 ≅ R_α. A (1−α)-polarization therefore amounts to Sym^k H¹ ≅ Γ^k H¹ as Γ_F-lattices, where k = n_α − 1; the twists match via the Weil pairing. Both are lattices in Sym^k V. For non-CM A_α the image of Γ_F is open in GL₂(ℤ_ℓ), so Sym^k V is absolutely irreducible, and an isomorphism would have to be a homothety. With the basis x^a y^{k−a}, the natural map to the divided powers is multiplication by a!(k−a)!. So the lattices are homothetic iff every binomial coefficient C(k,a) is prime to ℓ. That holds for k < ℓ and fails for ℓ ⩽ k ⩽ 2ℓ−2; examples are ℓ = 3 with n₀ = 4 (C(3,1) = 3) or n₁ = 5 (C(4,2) = 6). The first reading's 'ℓ = 3, n_α ⩾ 4' is slightly too broad. For n_α = 6 every C(5,a) is prime to 3, so a polarization exists; the same happens whenever k = dℓ^e − 1. Only large ℓ are used (Proposition 2.7.2, Lemma 8.1.3). Versions: same text in v1 and v3.

sourceIssues.locator: Construction 3.1.10, published p. 142; arXiv v3 p. 25; v1 p. 25
sourceIssues.printed: "Suppose that Π satisfies Π ∘ c ≃ Π∨. For v ∉ Σ+Π, the Satake parameter α(Πv) is unitary."
sourceIssues.correction: Assume in addition that the central character ω_Π is trivial on 𝔸_{F^+}^× (true for relevant Π). In general only α(Π_v) = α(Π_v)^{−1} as multisets holds, and at an inert v the product of the entries equals ω_Π(ϖ_v) = ±1.
sourceIssues.reason: At an unramified inert v, Π_w ∘ c ≃ Π_w^∨ and c(ϖ_v) = ϖ_v give α(Π_v) = α(Π_v)^{−1} as multisets. Hence (−T)^N P_α(T^{−1}) = (∏α_i)^{−1}P_α(T) with ∏α_i = ω_{Π_w}(ϖ_v). Since ω_Π ∘ c = ω_Π^{−1}, the restriction ω_Π|_{𝔸_{F^+}^×} is quadratic and trivial on norms, so it equals 1 or η_{F/F^+}; in the second case ω(ϖ_v) = −1 and α(Π_v) is not unitary. Explicit counterexample: N = 1, Π = χ a Hecke character of 𝔸_F^×/F^× extending η_{F/F^+} (it exists by Pontryagin duality). Then χ·χ^c = η ∘ Nm = 1, so χ ∘ c = χ^{−1}, but α(χ_v) = {−1} at every inert unramified v, and T + 1 ≠ (−T)(T^{−1} + 1). Defence: the construction is used only for relevant Π. There Definition 1.1.3(3) makes the archimedean central character arg^{Σ(N+1−2i)} = 1, which is incompatible with η_{F/F^+} (the sign character at each real place), so ω_Π|_{𝔸_{F^+}^×} = 1 and the claim holds. Independent check: Construction 3.1.10 checked on the image of p. 142, with Π cuspidal on GL_N(𝔸_F) (p. 138). At an inert unramified v, c(ϖ_v) = ϖ_v and Π∘c ≃ Π^∨ give α = α^{−1} as multisets. Hence (−T)^N P_α(T^{−1}) = (∏α_i)P_α(T), and unitarity (Definition 3.1.3(1)) is equivalent to ω_Π(ϖ_v) = 1. ω_Π restricted to 𝔸_{F⁺}^× is quadratic and trivial on norms, so it is 1 or η_{F/F⁺}. The counterexample works: χ extending η_{F/F⁺} exists by Pontryagin duality and is unramified almost everywhere by continuity. It satisfies χ∘c = χ^{−1}, and α(χ_v) = {−1} is not unitary for N = 1, since that would force α = {1}. For relevant Π (Definition 1.1.3(3)), the archimedean central character is arg^{Σ(N+1−2i)} = 1. This excludes η, which is the sign character at real places, so the claim holds wherever the construction is used. Versions: same in v1 and v3.

The footnote's condition is equivalent to something else: that some CM type Φ ∋ τ_∞ satisfies σ²Φ = Φ, i.e. ℚ_p^Φ = ℚ_{p²}, which is condition (P3)/(PI3) of §§6–7.

Then 17 = 𝔭𝔮 in F^+, with √2 ≡ 6 at 𝔭. At 𝔭, −3 + √2 ≡ 3 is a non-square mod 17, so 𝔭 is inert in F. At 𝔮, −3 + √2 ≡ 8 = 5², so 𝔮 splits in F. 17 is odd and unramified in F (the polynomial discriminant is 2^{10}·7), and 𝔭 has degree 1, so 𝔭 is special inert. The only prime above 17 that is inert in F is 𝔭, of odd degree 1, so the footnote declares 𝔭 very special. But the CM types of F are primitive with reflex fields of real quadratic subfield ℚ(√7) (√7 = √(−3+√2)·√(−3−√2)), so ⋂_Φ F_Φ = ℚ(√7). Hence F_rflx = F(√7) = M and F^+_rflx = ℚ(√2, √7). Since (7/17) = −1, 𝔭 is inert in F^+_rflx/F^+ and is not very special. (ii) Very special does not imply the footnote's condition. Take F a CM octic field with Gal(M/ℚ) = W(B_4) = (ℤ/2)^4 ⋊ S_4 (a generic F = F^+(√−δ) with F^+ an S_4-quartic). Then H = {(ε, π) : Σε_i even}, which has index 2 and contains c, so 𝔭 is very special iff the number of primes of F^+ above p that are inert in F is even. A Frobenius σ = ((1,1,0,0), (2 3)) (it exists by Chebotarev) gives 𝔭 inert of degree 1, 𝔮 inert of degree 2 and 𝔮′ split of degree 1. There are two inert primes, so 𝔭 is very special, but 𝔮 has even degree. Moreover σ² interchanges τ and τ^c for the embeddings above 𝔮, so no CM type is σ²-stable and (P3) fails. In the cases of Remark 1.1.8 (F Galois or containing an imaginary quadratic field) the definition and the footnote both reduce to 'special inert'. The footnote does mislead anyone checking hypothesis (a) of Theorem 1.1.7. Independent check: Footnote 11 and the definitions were checked on the image of p. 147. There the footnote condition is always equivalent to (P3), while 'very special' differs in both directions. (i) D₄: x⁴+6x²+7 has discriminant 2¹⁰·7. Mod 17 it factors as (x−5)(x+5)(x²−3), H = V₄ ∋ c, and ⋂F_Φ = ℚ(√7). Since (7/17) = −1, the degree-one prime inert in F is not very special, though it meets the footnote. sourceIssues.correction: (2) The restriction of ι to B_{s⋆} is unramified (i.e. étale-locally on B_{s⋆} a closed immersion), with normal bundle ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ∞}, im α_{*,τ∞}); it is a closed immersion when it is injective on geometric points, e.g. when K^p is sufficiently small (Remark 4.3.6).
sourceIssues.reason: The proof only shows that the tangent map T_{B_{s⋆}} → ι^*T_M is injective, i.e. that ι|B_{s⋆} is unramified. Zariski-locally a closed immersion fails whenever ι|B_{s⋆} is not injective on geometric points: B_{s⋆} is proper and irreducible (Theorem 4.3.5(3)), so any Zariski open U ∋ x is dense and ι(U) ∩ V must equal ι(B_{s⋆}) ∩ V for ι|U to be a closed immersion into an open V; if x′ ≠ x has ι(x′) = ι(x) = y, then ι(B_{s⋆}) has two branches at y (or ι is generically non-injective), while U is smooth at x, so U → ι(B_{s⋆}) ∩ V is not an isomorphism. Non-injectivity does occur: for N = 3 each superspecial point of M_𝔭 lies on p + 1 components ι(B_{s⋆}) indexed by the p + 1 neighbouring vertex lattices, and these p + 1 lattices give points of S_𝔭(V, K^p)(F̄_p) over one point of T_𝔭(F̄_p), a set in bijection with Sh(V⋆, (iK^p)K⋆_p) (Proposition 4.4.4); if p + 1 exceeds |Sh(V⋆, (iK^p)K⋆_p)|, two of them coincide and the corresponding B_{s⋆} passes twice through the superspecial point. Remark 4.3.6 (closed immersion for K^p sufficiently small) is consistent with this. Defence: 'locally' can be read étale-locally, which is what the proof gives; every later use (pure codimension ⌊N/2⌋, the normal bundle, the Gysin maps ι_! in Construction 4.4.9, transversality in Theorem 4.6.2) needs only unramifiedness, and in Proposition 4.5.5 the reduction still works: an unramified morphism from a smooth scheme that is bijective on geometric points and on tangent spaces is étale and universally injective, hence an isomorphism. Independent check: Quotation checked on pp. 166, 168, 180 (and Remark 4.3.6, p. 169: closed immersion only 'when K^p is sufficiently small'). The proof of (2) only shows T_{B_{s⋆}} → ι^*T_M injective, i.e. ι|B_{s⋆} unramified; p. 180 then uses (2) as 'locally for the Zariski topology on the source a closed immersion'. That reading is false as soon as ι|B_{s⋆} is not injective on geometric points. Independent proof: let x ≠ x′ in B := B_{s⋆} (over κ = F̄_p) with ι(x) = ι(x′) = y, and suppose U ∋ x is open with ι|U an immersion onto Z. B is proper and irreducible, so U is dense, Z is open in the closed set ι(B), Z = ι(B) ∩ V with V ⊆ M open, and W := B ∩ ι^{-1}(V) → Z is proper. The inverse Z ≅ U ⊆ W is a section of the separated map W → Z, so U is closed in W; it is also open and W is irreducible, hence U = W ∋ x′, contradicting injectivity of U → Z. Non-injectivity occurs: for N = 3 (Vollaard–Wedhorn picture) each superspecial point lies on p + 1 curves ι(B_{s⋆}) indexed by the p + 1 neighbouring vertex lattices, which share the prime-to-p component; if two are equivalent under U(V⋆)(F⁺) (γΛ₁ = Λ₂, γ ≠ 1 by neatness), the curve of Λ₁ passes through the superspecial point twice (at v and γ^{-1}v ≠ v). By pigeonhole this happens when p + 1 > |Sh(V⋆, (iK^p)K⋆_p)|, and for a fixed away-from-p level this cardinality does not grow with p (for odd N, K⋆_p is hyperspecial and the totally definite unitary group of rank 3 is independent of p up to isomorphism), so it happens for all large inert p. Case for the defence: read étale-locally, (2) is true (unramified ⇒ étale-locally a closed immersion, Stacks 04HJ); all later uses (codimension, normal bundle, Gysin maps, transversality) need only unramifiedness, and in Proposition 4.5.5 the reduction still works (a morphism of smooth schemes bijective on geometric points and on tangent spaces is étale and universally injective, hence an isomorphism). So the statement is wrong in the sense the paper itself uses, with no downstream damage.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.3.4(3), published p. 285
sourceIssues.printed: Part (3) is a consequence of (1) and (P4) that P_{α(Π_𝔭)} mod λ^m is level-raising special at 𝔭. In fact, we have an isomorphism H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄•_N, O_λ(r)) ≃ H ⊗_{R^ram} R_1(r) of O_λ[Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})]-modules.
sourceIssues.correction: Read the left side as localised at 𝔪, and let R_1 ⊆ (R^ram)^{⊕N} be the r^♮_ram(φ_p²)-stable complement of R^ram v ⊕ R^ram v′; inertia acts trivially on it. Then H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄•_N, O_λ(r))_𝔪 = E_2^{0,2r−1} = Gr_0 H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ(r))_𝔪 ≅ H ⊗_{R^ram} R_1(r). Proof: (a) F_{−1} and H/F_0 (E_2^{1,2r−2} and E_2^{−1,2r}) have Frobenius eigenvalues p² and 1 by Lemma 5.6.2. By (P4) these are separated modulo λ from the eigenvalues on R_1(r), so H ⊗ R_1(r) ⊆ Gr_0. (b) The {1,p²}-block has zero image in Gr_0: rationally because the monodromy x is nonzero at every characteristic-zero point of R^ram, and integrally because Gr_0 is O_λ-free by part (2).
sourceIssues.reason: The symbol R_1 appears nowhere else in the paper, and the displayed isomorphism — which is the entire content of the proof of (3) — is asserted without argument. Defence: with the reading above the isomorphism holds and gives (3): the eigenvalues of r^♮_ram(φ_p²) on R_1 are p^{1−2r}α_i^{±1} (i ≠ the level-raising index), and twisting by ε_ℓ(φ_p²)^r = p^{2r} gives pα_i^{±1}, avoiding 1 and p². Independent check: Quote checked on p. 285: 'Part (3) is a consequence of (1) and (P4) … In fact, we have an isomorphism H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄•_N, O_λ(r)) ≃ H ⊗_{R^ram} R_1(r) of O_λ[Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})]-modules.' In the text layer of pub/v1/v2/v3, R_1 occurs only in this line, so it is never defined. The left side also lacks the localisation at 𝔪 that part (3) concerns. The displayed isomorphism is all the proof of (3) has, and it is not immediate. By Lemma 5.9.3(1), E_1^{0,2r−1} = H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄•_N, L(r)) and the odd-degree terms of M°, M† vanish, so H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄•_N)_𝔪 = E_2^{0,2r−1} = Gr_0 of H^{2r−1}_𝔪 ≅ H ⊗ (R^ram)^{⊕N}(r) (p. 282). To identify Gr_0 with H ⊗ (complement of R^ram v ⊕ R^ram v′)(r) one needs three things. (i) Frobenius eigenvalues. E_2^{−1,2r} ⊆ H^{2r−2}(M̄†, L(r−1)) and E_2^{1,2r−2}, a quotient of H^{2r−2}(M̄†, L(r)), have Frobenius eigenvalues 1 and p² (Lemma 5.6.2). By (P4) these are separated modulo λ from the eigenvalues p·α_i^{±1} (i ≠ the level-raising index) on the complement, so the complement lies in Gr_0. (ii) The {1, p²}-block H ⊗ (R^ram v ⊕ R^ram v′)(r) contributes nothing to Gr_0. This needs a further argument. For example: at every characteristic-zero point of R^ram ≅ T^ram_𝔪, the monodromy x is nonzero (nontrivial monodromy at 𝔭, cf. p. 277), so the block has no Gr_0 rationally, and Gr_0 is O_λ-free by (2). (iii) The complement on which inertia acts trivially must actually be named. The first reading's reading (R_1 = the φ²-stable complement, i.e. M_1 of [51]) makes the isomorphism true, and (3) then follows. But the paper supplies neither the definition nor steps (i)–(ii), so this is a gap, not a misprint. Versions: the same line is in v1/v2 p. 120 and v3 p. 119.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.3.4(5), published pp. 285–286
sourceIssues.printed: We claim that O_λ/λ^m = R^ram/𝔫 … Since 𝔫 satisfies 𝔫 ∩ O_λ = λ^m O_λ, the structure homomorphism O_λ → R^ram induces an equality O_λ/λ^m = R^ram/𝔫.
sourceIssues.correction: Add to Theorem 6.3.4(5) the hypothesis that P_{α(Π_v)} mod λ^m is level-raising special at v (Definition 3.1.5) for every v ∈ Σ⁺_lr. Equivalently, ρ̄^{(m)}_{Π,λ,+} satisfies 𝒟^ram at Σ⁺_lr; this holds vacuously if Σ⁺_lr = ∅. In the proof, read 𝔫 O_λ-linearly, as the kernel of O_λ ⊗ T^{Σ⁺∪Σ⁺_p}_N → O_λ/λ^m. With these, ρ_{Π,λ,+} mod λ^m is of type 𝒮^ram, and so R^ram/𝔫 = O_λ/λ^m. The added hypothesis holds in both applications: Theorem 8.2.2 (Σ⁺_lr = ∅) and Theorem 8.3.2 (Σ⁺_lr = {𝔭_1}, by (PII4)).
sourceIssues.reason: As defined in Notation 6.1.3, 𝔫 is an ideal of the ℤ[‖v‖^{±1/2}]-algebra T^{Σ⁺∪Σ⁺_p}_N; read literally, λ^m need not lie in 𝔫R^ram when E_λ is ramified over the field generated by the Hecke eigenvalues. Read O_λ-linearly, R^ram/𝔫 is a quotient O_λ/λ^j of O_λ/λ^m, and j = m requires an O_λ-algebra map R^ram → O_λ/λ^m compatible with φ_Π, i.e. (Chebotarev and Carayol) that ρ_{Π,λ} mod λ^m be a lifting of type 𝒮^ram. At 𝔭 this is (P4) (mod λ^m); but at v ∈ Σ⁺_lr the local condition is 𝒟^ram, which demands P_0(T) = (T − ‖v‖^{−N})(T − ‖v‖^{−N+2}) exactly ([51, Definition 3.5.1]), whereas the hypotheses of Theorem 6.3.4 (rigidity (b), §6.1) only give this modulo λ. If Π_v is level-raising special only modulo λ^j with j < m, then R^ram/𝔫 = O_λ/λ^{j′} with j′ ⩽ j, H^{2r−1}/𝔫 ≅ H ⊗ (R^ram/𝔫)^{⊕N}(r) is killed by λ^{j′} (and nonzero since d_ram > 0), and the conclusion (R̄^{(m)c})^{⊕μ} with μ ⩾ 1 fails. Defence: in the applications (§8, pp. 318–319) Σ⁺_lr is either ∅ or {𝔭_1} with 𝔭_1 a previously chosen prime satisfying (PII4), i.e. level-raising special modulo λ^m, so the main theorems are unaffected; Theorem 6.3.4(4) is unaffected.
